chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad, from Ishaq ibn Muhammad, from Yahya ibn al-Muthanna, from ‘Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:
I heard Aba ‘Abdillah (عليه السلام) saying: “The people will lose sight of their Imam. He attends the season, so he sees them, while they do not see him.”

key_terms.إِمَامَهُمْ: their Imam, the divinely appointed leader
key_terms.النَّاسُ: the people or community at large
key_terms.الْمَوْسِمَ: the pilgrimage season, especially the time of Hajj
key_terms.وَلَا يَرَوْنَهُ: while they do not see him
key_terms.يَفْقِدُ: to lose or be deprived of direct access to

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the Imam’s presence during the occultation?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a state in which the people are deprived of direct access to their Imam, even though he remains present among them. It indicates that during the season of Hajj, the Imam witnesses the people while remaining unrecognized by them, reflecting the doctrine of ghaybah (occultation) in Shia theology.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad, from Is’haq Bin Muhammad, from Yahya Bin Al Musna, from Abdullah Bin Bukeyr, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The people would miss their Imam<sup>asws</sup>. He<sup>asws</sup> would be attending the season (Hajj), so he<sup>asws</sup> would see them and they would not see him<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ja’far ibn Muhammad from Ishaq ibn Muhammad from Yahya ibn al-Muthanna from ‘Abdallah ibn Bukayr from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurara who has said the following.
“I heard abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) say as herein below. “People will miss their Imam (a.s.). He will attain Hajj and see them but they will not see him.”
